original_question: For an equivariant map Lie algebra M = M(X, g)^Gamma, compute higher extension groups between finite-dimensional modules, not just Ext^1, and explain how those higher Ext groups and the global dimension of the finite-dimensional module category depend on the geometry of the scheme X.
target_in_paper: Section 4.3.1(a), "Higher extensions," the open problem asking for higher Ext-groups for equivariant map Lie algebras and for the relation between those groups, the geometry of X, and the global dimension of the finite-dimensional module category. The nearby technical context is Theorem 3.2 and §3.2, especially Proposition 3.5. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the core problem very well: it stays in the Lie EMA setting M = M(X, g)^Γ, asks for higher Ext-groups beyond the Ext^1 theory already available, and explicitly includes the two features singled out by the paper itself—dependence on the geometry of X and the global dimension of the category of finite-dimensional modules. That is exactly the thrust of §4.3.1(a). ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))
missing_details: The paper frames this as a continuation of the known Ext^1 description for irreducible finite-dimensional modules, so "finite-dimensional modules" in your draft is slightly broader than the paper's immediate target; the sharp paper-faithful formulation should name irreducible finite-dimensional M-modules first. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))

The ambient setup should be stated explicitly: X = Spec A is an affine scheme, Γ is a finite group, M = M(X, g)^Γ = (g ⊗ A)^Γ, and in the Lie-theoretic parts of the paper k is algebraically closed of characteristic 0. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))

To make the question stand alone in the paper's own language, it helps to note that irreducible finite-dimensional M-modules are classified in §3.1 as one-dimensional twists of evaluation modules; that is the representation-theoretic class whose Ext^1 theory is being extended. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))

The existing Ext^1 results summarized in §3.2 are stated under extra hypotheses (there A is finitely generated and g is reductive), and the especially geometric formula in Proposition 3.5 assumes in addition that g is semisimple, Γ is abelian, and Γ acts freely on Xrat. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))

The phrase "depend on the geometry of X" is not meant abstractly only: the nearby motivating example is Proposition 3.5, where the Zariski tangent space (mx/mx^2)^* at a rational point x appears explicitly. A refined question should mention that local geometric input. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))

The paper's wording is about the global dimension of the category of finite-dimensional M-modules specifically, so that category should be named exactly. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))
refined_question: Let M = M(X, g)^Γ = (g ⊗ A)^Γ be an equivariant map Lie algebra, where X = Spec A is an affine scheme over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic 0 and Γ is a finite group. For irreducible finite-dimensional M-modules V and V' (equivalently, by Theorem 3.2, one-dimensional twists of evaluation modules), determine the higher extension groups ExtM^n(V, V') for all n ≥ 2, extending the Ext^1 theory summarized in §3.2 and, in particular, the geometric behavior exemplified by Proposition 3.5 through the tangent space (mx/mx^2)^*; furthermore, determine how these higher Ext-groups and the global dimension of the category of finite-dimensional M-modules are related to the geometry of X. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))
justification: The draft is clearly targeting the open problem in §4.3.1(a), not a neighboring problem. The decisive phrases from your draft—"higher extension groups," their dependence on the geometry of X, and the "global dimension" of the finite-dimensional module category—match the wording of §4.3.1(a) almost verbatim. The nearby context that makes this precise is: the general Lie EMA setup in §4.3; the classification of irreducible finite-dimensional modules in Theorem 3.2; and the Ext^1 formulas of §3.2, especially Proposition 3.5, where the tangent space provides the model example of how geometry enters. ([alistairsavage.ca](https://alistairsavage.ca/pubs/neher-savage-2013-conm602-EMA_survey.pdf))
